Interpreting the FOMC statement through standard monetary-policy frameworks still points to a mildly positive but cautious tone (solid growth, strong labor market, gradual hikes, and technical normalization). However, the October 2017 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey tempers that positivity via the credit channel. Banks reported easing standards for some commercial and industrial loans amid competition, but also tightened terms for consumer credit—especially credit cards and auto loans—while demand weakened across multiple categories (credit cards, auto, inventory and A/R financing, capex, and M&A). Reasons cited for tightening included the economic outlook, loan portfolio quality, and risk tolerance. Although banks indicated willingness to make consumer installment loans, the broader picture is of mixed-to-soft credit conditions that could restrain household and business spending at the margin.

Netting the strong labor market and “solid” growth against sub-2% inflation and SLOOS evidence of tightening in key consumer segments and weaker loan demand, the overall tone shifts from mildly positive to slightly positive/cautious.
